newsitem.title: USA: Firm asks AutoInfo to change poison pill.
newsitem.headline: Firm asks AutoInfo to change poison pill.

text.p: Steel Partners II LP said Monday it asked AutoInfo Inc to amend its "poison pill" antitakeover provision or remove it entirely so the partnership could raise its stake to more than 15 percent.
Steel Partners, the largest shareholder in AutoInfo with a 14.2 percent stake, also urged the AutoInfo board to launch a share repurchase plan as a way of raising value of the stock to shareholders.
The partnership made its recommendations in a letter to AutoInfo on September 16, according to its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The partnership said its plan to raise its stake "reflects our confidence and belief that significant value could be realized for the benefit of all stockholders."
It said it bought its stake beginning last year when AutoInfo's stock was trading at $3.35, which it believe was already a discount to net cash and book value.

At the same time, it added that with the (current) stock price at $2.00, one of the best uses of the company's cash would be to make an investment in its own shares through a stock repurchase program.

A poison pill is a rights agreement that allows shareholders to buy shares in the company at a steep discount if a hostile holder or group breaches a stated ownership limit. The effect is to make it prohibitively expensive for the hostile investor to mount a takeover.
